Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As we kick off the AureliaCare pilot, our security and privacy folks asked for a concise inventory that covers:

- a processing topology diagram showing each component that can touch PII (ingest, proxy, inference, logs, exports)

Elena, hi — attaching the first-pass artifacts.

Attachments:
- processing_topology_v1.drawio (diagram stub)
- pii-field-inventory.csv (field-level mapping)

High-level notes (quick answers up front):
- Scope: initial pack covers production inference pathway only. If you need staging/dev, say so and we'll include those lanes.
- PII fields: inventory contains columns (field_name, example, classification, retention_default). See pii-field-inventory.csv for samples (email, name, account_id, free-form notes).
- Access zoning: internal access is RBAC-based.
  - Product/Support: role-limited, no raw PII in support tools by default; access requires Just-In-Time elevation and an access ticket.
  - SRE/Infra: can access runtime logs (non-PII) and aggregated metrics; PII is redacted unless a justified debug session is opened and approved by security.
- KMS & key custody: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via standard KMS providers; when BYOK is used, customer keys are in your KMS and Redwood stores only a reference. We attached a short attestation stub later in the thread for KMS practices.
- Subprocessors: primary infra partner is CloudPartnerX (EU region presence). They operate at the VM/hosting layer and do not have application-level access to plaintext PII in normal operations; network egress is controlled and contractually bounded (SCCs in place).

I've also uploaded the diagram to our onboarding drive: https://redwood.app/drive/onboarding/aureliacare/topology-v1

If you want, Connor can add the runbook excerpts for retention and log anonymization.

Thanks,

Also attaching a short DPA redline guidance doc from legal; we'll mark up items related to retention and routing.

Hi Elena,

Quick answers to your ops questions:

- Logs: by default, runtime traces and operational logs do NOT persist raw model inputs/outputs. We have two categories:
  1) Telemetry/metrics: token counts, latency, error rates (no PII).
  2) Debug snapshots: captured only with customer approval or an elevated support session; those are redacted automatically where possible, and any capture is logged in our access log.

- Retention: standard diagnostics/telemetry retention is 30 days. Audit logs (access and admin events) are retained for 13 months. Any extension beyond default retention (e.g., 90d or permanent export) is available under contract amendment in the DPA/annex.

- Region pinning: strict-region pinning is available via Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private deployments. Hosted (shared) API can be routed by region but cannot guarantee hard-disk locality unless you select a dedicated/ private plan and contractually bind egress rules.

- Subprocessors: we'll provide a current roster in a one-page table. Short note: CloudPartnerX (IaaS) and ObservabilityVendorY (metrics) are in the chain. None have application-level access under normal operations; we share the subprocessor roles and contract mappings in the DPA annex.

I've attached a short KMS attestation stub for your security team to reference.

Attachment: kms-attestation-stub.pdf

Next step: propose a 30-minute technical sync (we can run through the diagram and the DPA redlines). I'm available Mon/Tue mornings 9-11 PT.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
